newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil continues trade at week's higher rang.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil continues trade at week's higher rang.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges remained steady early on Wednesday in the higher range of the past two days, but traders said the higher numbers were not backed by strong demand.
High sulphur barges were done early at $84.50 in two trades for 1,000 tonnes each then 1,000 tonnes were done at $85 fob ARA, or Tuesday's closing level.
Later offers were said to be in the $86 region for refining material and $85 for storage.
However, a Rotterdam trader was offering high sulphur fuel directly off a ship at $84.50, traders said.
"Demand is lousy, some 6,000 to 9,000 tonnes," one trader said. A second trader said bunker demand was 10,000 tonnes by midday.
"The market is exceptionally quiet. There were very small trades at high numbers, like in the past two days," he said, adding that many in the market were in a wait-and-see mode.
Low sulphur barges were also unchanged, with one trader saying: "It is still talked at $95/$97 (a tonne fob). There are no close discussions, buyers and sellers are still apart".
